p.THE-PROJECT-USES-THE-ATOMIC-COMMITS-DISC: This project uses the **atomic commits** discipline as its Git contract.

p.ONE-COMMIT-ONE-IDEA-AND-THE-MESSAGE-EXPL: One commit carries exactly one idea, and the commit message explains *why*.

p.ONE-COMMIT-EQUALS-ONE-LOGICAL-CHANGE: **One commit = one logical change**, not one file changed.

p.A-MIXED-SESSION-IS-THREE-COMMITS: A session that produces (a) a typo fix, (b) a refactor, and (c) a schema update is **three** commits, not one.

p.A-COHERENT-FIFTEEN-FILE-CHANGE-IS-ONE-CO: A feature that touches fifteen files for one coherent reason is **one** commit, not fifteen.

p.COMMIT-MESSAGES-FOLLOW-THE-CONVENTIONAL-: Commit messages follow the **git-conventional-commits** flow — a sibling package: `spec://org.vibevm.world/git-conventional-commits/flows/conventional-commits/conventional-commits#root`.

p.CONVENTIONAL-COMMITS-IS-THE-FORMAT-THIS-: Conventional Commits is the *format*; this flow is the *atomicity* (one commit, one idea).

p.THE-TWO-ARE-DISTINCT-AND-RUN-TOGETHER: The two are distinct and run together — a `feat: add foo, bar, baz` message is valid Conventional Commits and a violation of the atomic rule.

item.STEP-RUN-STATUS-AND-DIFF-AND-NAME-EVERY-: Run `git status` and `git diff HEAD`. Name every change by intent.

item.STEP-GROUP-CHANGES-INTO-ATOMIC-COMMITS: Group changes into atomic commits — one commit per intent, not per file.

item.STEP-STAGE-AND-COMMIT-EACH-GROUP-SEPARAT: Stage and commit each group separately with a well-formed message.

item.STEP-DO-NOT-AMEND-OR-FORCE-PUSH-PUSHED-C: Do not amend or force-push commits that are already pushed; create a new commit instead, unless the human explicitly approves history rewriting.

p.splitting-procedure-pointer: Procedure for splitting a messy working tree: @spec://org.vibevm.world/git-atomic-commits/flows/atomic-commits/splitting-large-changes#root.

why-human-ai-teams.title: Why this matters in a human-AI team

item.WHY-DIFF-AS-VERIFICATION: **Diff as verification.** Humans verify code by reading diffs. A diff that mixes three concerns is not verifiable in one pass.

item.WHY-ROLLBACK-PRECISION: **Rollback precision.** `git revert <sha>` must undo the wrong thing without also undoing two correct things.

item.WHY-COMMIT-LOG-AS-DECISION-RECORD: **Commit log as decision record.** The message is the only place where *why* survives after the WAL and spec prose decay.

item.NEVER-MIX-REFACTOR-FEATURE-DOCS-AND-BUGF: Never mix refactor + feature + docs + bugfix in one commit.

item.NEVER-WRITE-A-SUBJECT-THAT-SUMMARISES-WH: Never write a subject that summarises *what* changed — the diff does that. Write *why*.

item.NEVER-AMEND-A-PUSHED-COMMIT-WITHOUT-HUMA: Never `git commit --amend` on a pushed commit without explicit human approval. Same for `git push --force`.
